column1: # BUCKET 3, ONE LINE PER ROW: the page address of every read-direction
# still-GAP row that scripts/census_completion.py counts as "blocked on nothing
# at all", and what the SHIPPED read boundary says about that address.
# Method, the class definitions and every finding:
# Checked by scripts/check_read_addresses.py, which re-drives every address
# below through readonly.is_read_url and exits 1 on any disagreement, on any
# bucket-3 row with no line here, on any line for a row that has left the
# bucket, on any source (file, ::SYMBOL, census row) that no longer
# resolves, and -- since 2026-09-23 -- on any row blocked on nothing whose
# page a ruling holds (scripts/ruling_holds.py names those rulings and where
# each binds). census_completion.py counts the class column; it does not
# is_read_url and refusal are MEASUREMENTS, re-taken on every check. Every
# other column is a JUDGEMENT, and each row names its source.
# EVERY VARIABLE SEGMENT IS A PLACEHOLDER -- placeholder-org, placeholder-school,
# The allowlist patterns accept a SHAPE, not a value, so no verdict depends on
# the value standing there, and no real identifier ever enters this file.
# class        ADMITTED | REFUSED | NO-ADDRESS | NEEDS-SESSION | UNDETERMINED
# basis        MEASURED  the address was seen served, or drawn on a live page
#              NAMED     written in code, a test, the census or an audit, and
#              INFERRED  constructed as representative, by a prior wave or
#                        this one; the row says which
# refusal      the shipped refusal's kind, read off assert_read_url:
# gate         ADMITTED rows only: the first thing past the boundary --
#              READER | PRESS-PERMITTED | MEASURE | BUILT-UNFIRED | PRESS | RULING
#              RULING is a decision nobody has made. STANDING-RULING is one
#              that HAS been made and holds the page; the note cites it as
#              HELD BY `<ID>`. READER and PRESS-PERMITTED are "blocked on
#              nothing", and may never sit on a page a ruling holds.
# also_driven  other addresses the corpus names for the row, each re-driven:
